purpose: Neratinib is used to treat a certain type of early-stage breast cancer that tests positive for a protein called HER2. It is taken after you have already completed treatment with another HER2-targeted medicine called trastuzumab (Herceptin). It helps lower the chance of the cancer coming back.
how_it_works: Cancer cells sometimes have a protein called HER2 on their surface that helps them grow out of control. Neratinib works like a key that blocks this protein, slowing down or stopping the cancer cells from growing and multiplying. Think of it as putting a lock on the switch that tells cancer cells to keep dividing.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea is the most common and can be severe — your doctor will likely give you anti-diarrhea medicine to take with it. Other common side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness, decreased appetite, mouth sores, and rash. Liver enzyme levels in your blood may also go up.
warnings: Diarrhea can be very serious and lead to dehydration, so it is very important to take anti-diarrhea medicine as directed and drink plenty of fluids. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so do not become pregnant while taking it and use effective birth control. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain, as these could be signs of liver problems.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 6 tablets (240 mg total) taken by mouth once a day with food. Treatment is typically continued for one year. It is important to take it at the same time each day and not to crush or chew the tablets.
